newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC hits all-time high on warrant talk.
newsitem.headline: HSBC hits all-time high on warrant talk.

text.p: Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc surged to an all-time high on Wednesday on buying fuelled by anticipation of strong earnings growth and talk of two covered warrant issues on the stock, brokers said.
"Anticipation of earnings growth of about 20 percent and talk of covered warrant issues on the bank fuelled buying," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.

HSBC shares rose HK$6.50 or 3.81 percent to an all-time high of HK$177 in late Wednesday morning trade before falling back slightly to HK$176.50, up HK$6.00. Volume was a heavy 3.646 million shares worth HK$637.42 million.
"We expect the shares to be fully valued at the HK$197 to HK$198 level," Li said.
Brokers said there was talk that at least three merchant banks are planning covered warrant issues on or involving HSBC.
HSBC is expected to release its final results on March 3.
